what_its_for: Gefitinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a certain type of lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It works best in patients whose cancer has a specific change (mutation) in a gene called EGFR. Your doctor will test your cancer cells to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food — it does not matter. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. If you have trouble swallowing the tablet, you can dissolve it in half a glass of plain (still) water. Stir it until the tablet breaks apart, drink it right away, and then rinse the glass with more water and drink that too. Do not crush or split the tablet in any other way.
dosing: The usual dose is one 250 mg tablet taken once a day, every day. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions — do not take more or less than prescribed. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 12 hours away. If your next dose is less than 12 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store gefitinib at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original packaging, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of them.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids or heartburn medicines (like omeprazole, lansoprazole, ranitidine, or Tums) around the same time as gefitinib, as they can make it less effective — ask your doctor or pharmacist for guidance. Avoid taking herbal supplements like St. John's Wort, as it can make the medicine stop working properly. Limit your time in the sun and use sunscreen, since this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant should avoid handling crushed or broken tablets.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: sudden or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever (possible lung problem); severe diarrhea (more than 6 loose stools per day) or stomach pain; eye pain, redness, or vision changes; skin rash that is severe, blistering, or peeling; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or severe tiredness; nausea or vomiting that you cannot control. Also tell your doctor about any new or unusual symptoms, as well as all other medicines, vitamins, or supplements you are taking.
when_it_works: Gefitinib does not work overnight. It may take several weeks to months before you or your doctor can see whether the medicine is working. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups and tests, such as scans or blood work. Even if you feel well, keep taking your medicine every day unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Gefitinib can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use contraception during treatment. Liver problems: If you have liver disease, your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your dose. Older adults: No dose adjustment is usually needed based on age alone, but tell your doctor about all your health conditions. Children: Gefitinib is not approved for use in children.
